title.raw: 卷一百十七 志第七十 禮二十 Volume 117 Treatises 70: Rites 20

sentences.zh: 禮二十

translations.literal: Rites 20
translations.idiomatic: Rites 20

sentences.zh: （賓禮二）〉

translations.literal: (Guest Rites II)›
translations.idiomatic: (Guest Rites II)›

sentences.zh: ○入閣儀明堂聽政儀肆赦儀附皇太后垂簾儀皇太子正至受賀儀皇太子與百官師保相見儀

translations.literal: ○ Entering-the-Pavilion Rites; Hall of Enlightened Rule Audience Rites; General Amnesty Rites; appended—Empress Dowager Curtain-Audience Rites; Crown Prince Winter Solstice Reception-of-Congratulations Rites; Crown Prince Meeting with Hundred Officials, Tutors, and Guardians Rites
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ceremonies for Entering the Pavilion, for Audiences at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, for General Amnesties, for the Empress Dowager Behind the Curtain, for the Crown Prince Receiving Congratulations at the Winter Solstice, and for the Crown Prince Meeting His Tutors, Guardians, and the Hundred Officials

sentences.zh: 入閣儀。

translations.literal: Entering-the-Pavilion Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Entering-the-Pavilion Rites.

sentences.zh: 唐制：天子日御正衙以見群臣，必立仗。

translations.literal: Tang institution: daily the Son of Heaven held court in the main administrative hall to see the hundred officials, and the guard of honor had to be posted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, the emperor held daily court in the main administrative hall to receive the hundred officials, and a guard of honor was always posted.

sentences.zh: 朔望薦食陵寢，不能臨前殿，則御便殿，乃自正衙喚仗由宣政兩門而入，是謂東、西上閣門，群臣俟於正衙者因隨以入，故謂之入閣。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of the month, when offerings were presented at the imperial tombs, he could not attend the front hall; then he held court in the convenience hall, summoned the guard of honor from the main hall to enter through the Xuanzheng east and west gates—this is what was called the eastern and western upper-pavilion gates; officials waiting in the main hall followed in and entered, hence it was called entering the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On new and full moon days, when food offerings were made at the imperial tombs, the emperor could not attend the front hall and instead held court in the convenience hall. He would summon the guard posted at the main hall to enter through the east and west upper-pavilion gates of Xuanzheng, and the officials waiting in the main hall followed him in; hence the ceremony was called entering the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，正衙既廢，而入閣亦希闊不講，宋復行之。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward the main administrative hall was abolished, and entering the pavilion was also rarely practiced and neglected; the Song restored it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward the main administrative hall fell out of use, and entering the pavilion was seldom observed; the Song revived the practice.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年四月朔，常服通天冠、絳紗袍，御崇元殿視朝，設金吾仗衛，群臣入閣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, on the first day of the fourth month, wearing ordinary dress, the open-topped cap, and crimson gauze robe, he held court in the Chongyuan Hall, posted the Golden Guard honor guard, and the hundred officials entered the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande, on the first day of the fourth month, the emperor wore ordinary dress with the open-topped cap and crimson gauze robe, held court in the Chongyuan Hall, posted the Golden Guard honor guard, and the hundred officials performed the entering-the-pavilion rite.

sentences.zh: 太宗淳化二年十一月，詔以十二月朔御文德殿入閣，令史館修撰楊徽之、張洎定為新儀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Chunhua, Emperor Taizong decreed that on the first day of the twelfth month he would hold entering-the-pavilion court in the Wende Hall, and ordered Academician-Compiler Yang Huizhi and Zhang Bi to draft the new protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Chunhua, Emperor Taizong decreed that on the first day of the twelfth month he would hold entering-the-pavilion court in the Wende Hall and ordered Academicians-Compiler Yang Huizhi and Zhang Bi to draft new regulations.

sentences.zh: 前一日，有司供帳於文德殿

translations.literal: On the day before, the relevant offices prepared the pavilion at the Wende Hall
translations.idiomatic: On the day before, the relevant offices prepared the pavilion at the Wende Hall

sentences.zh: （宋初曰「文明」）〉

translations.literal: (In the early Song it was called "Wenming")›
translations.idiomatic: (In the early Song it was called "Wenming")›

sentences.zh: 是日既明，先列文武官於殿庭之東西，百官、軍校、行軍副使等序班於正衙門外屏南階下；

translations.literal: When day broke that day, civil and military officials were first arrayed east and west in the hall courtyard; the hundred officials, military officers, deputy field-commanders, and the like formed ranks south of the steps on the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;
translations.idiomatic: When day broke, civil and military officials were first arrayed east and west in the hall courtyard, while the hundred officials, military officers, deputy field-commanders, and the like formed ranks south of the steps on the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;

sentences.zh: 次御史中丞、三院御史序立，中丞獨穿金吾班過揖兩班，一揖歸本位；

translations.literal: next the Vice Censor-in-Chief and censors of the three bureaus took their places in order; the Vice Censor-in-Chief alone passed through the Golden Guard formation, bowed to both ranks, bowed once, and returned to his position;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Vice Censor-in-Chief and censors of the three bureaus took their places; the Vice Censor-in-Chief alone passed through the Golden Guard formation, bowed to both ranks, bowed once, and returned to his position;

sentences.zh: 次監察御史兩員監閣，於正衙門外屏北階上北面立；

translations.literal: next two investigating censors supervised the pavilion gate, standing facing north on the northern steps of the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;
translations.idiomatic: Next two investigating censors supervised the pavilion gate, standing facing north on the northern steps of the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、文明翰林樞密直學士、兩省官分班立；

translations.literal: next officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Wenming Hall, Hanlin, and Privy Council direct academicians, and officials of the two departments formed ranks separately;
translations.idiomatic: Next officials of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Wenming Hall, Hanlin, and Privy Council direct academicians, and officials of the two departments formed separate ranks;

sentences.zh: 次司天奏辰刻；

translations.literal: next the Astronomical Bureau reported the double-hour;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Astronomical Bureau reported the double-hour;

sentences.zh: 次閣門版奏班齊。

translations.literal: next the Pavilion Gate reported on the tally board that the ranks were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Pavilion Gate reported on the tally board that the ranks were complete.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服靴袍乘輦，至長春殿駐輦，樞密使以下奏謁，前導至文德殿。

translations.literal: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, rode in the palanquin to the Changchun Hall and halted the palanquin; from the Commissioner of Military Affairs downward they announced their audience, and led the way to the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, rode in the palanquin to the Changchun Hall and halted; from the Commissioner of Military Affairs downward they announced their audience and led the way to the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 殿上承旨索扇，卷簾。

translations.literal: On the dais the designated recipient called for fans; the screens were rolled up.
translations.idiomatic: On the dais the designated recipient called for fans, and the screens were rolled up.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升位，扇卻，儀鸞使焚香；

translations.literal: the emperor ascended the seat; the fans were withdrawn; the Ceremonial Guard commissioner burned incense;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the seat; the fans were withdrawn; the Ceremonial Guard commissioner burned incense;

sentences.zh: 次文武官等拜；

translations.literal: next the civil and military officials bowed;
translations.idiomatic: Next the civil and military officials bowed;

sentences.zh: 次司天雞唱；

translations.literal: next the Astronomical Bureau's rooster crow was intoned;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Astronomical Bureau's rooster crow was intoned;

sentences.zh: 次閣門勘契；

translations.literal: next the Pavilion Gate verified the tallies;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Pavilion Gate verified the tallies;

sentences.zh: 次閣門使承旨呼四色官喚仗，南班有辭謝者再拜先退，中書、門下班對揖，序立正衙門外屏北階上；

translations.literal: next the Pavilion Gate commissioner, upon receiving the order, summoned the four-color officials to call out the guard of honor; those in the southern rank who had farewell speeches bowed twice and withdrew first; the Secretariat and Chancellery ranks bowed to each other and took their places in order on the northern steps of the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Pavilion Gate commissioner, upon receiving the order, summoned the four-color officials to call out the guard of honor; those in the southern rank with farewell speeches bowed twice and withdrew first; the Secretariat and Chancellery ranks bowed to each other and took their places on the northern steps of the screen outside the main administrative hall gate;

sentences.zh: 次翰林學士、兩省官、中丞、侍御史序立；

translations.literal: next Hanlin academicians, officials of the two departments, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, and attendant censors took their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: Next Hanlin academicians, officials of the two departments, the Vice Censor-in-Chief, and attendant censors took their places in order;

sentences.zh: 次金吾將軍押細仗入正衙門後，橫行拜訖，分行上黃道，仗隨入，金吾將軍至龍墀分班揖訖，序立；

translations.literal: next the Golden Guard general escorted the detail guard through the main administrative hall gate; after crossing and bowing, they split ranks and went up the yellow path, the guard following in; the Golden Guard general reached the dragon terrace, divided ranks, finished bowing, and took their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Golden Guard general escorted the detail guard through the main administrative hall gate; after crossing and bowing, they split ranks and went up the yellow path with the guard following; the Golden Guard general reached the dragon terrace, divided ranks, finished bowing, and took their places in order;

sentences.zh: 次吏部、兵部侍郎執文武班簿入，對揖立；

translations.literal: next the Vice Ministers of Personnel and of War entered carrying the civil and military rank registers, bowed to each other, and stood;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Vice Ministers of Personnel and of War entered carrying the civil and military rank registers, bowed to each other, and stood;

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、學士、兩省、御史台官入，北面拜訖，上黃道，將至午階，𣀃𣀃鞾急趨赴丹墀，彈奏御史至吏部侍郎南便落黃道，急趨就位；

translations.literal: next officials of the Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, two departments, and Censorate entered, bowed facing north, went up the yellow path; as they neared the noon steps they hurried in boots with quick steps to the cinnabar terrace; the impeachment censor to the Vice Minister of Personnel's south side left the yellow path and hurried to take their places;
translations.idiomatic: Next officials of the Secretariat, Chancellery, academicians, two departments, and Censorate entered, bowed facing north, and went up the yellow path; as they neared the noon steps they hurried in boots with quick steps to the cinnabar terrace; the impeachment censor, reaching the south side of the Vice Minister of Personnel, left the yellow path and hurried to take his place;

sentences.zh: 起居郎、舍人至兵部、吏部侍郎後，急趨而進，飛至香案前，皆揖訖序立；

translations.literal: the court diarists and heralds, following the Vice Ministers of War and Personnel, hurried forward, flew to before the incense table, all bowed, and took their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: The court diarists and heralds, following the Vice Ministers of War and Personnel, hurried forward to the incense table, bowed, and took their places in order;

sentences.zh: 次金吾大將軍先對揖並鞠躬，𣀃鞾行至折方石位又對揖，北行至奏事石位鞠躬，一員奏軍國內外平安，倒行就位；

translations.literal: next the Grand General of the Golden Guard first bowed face to face and bent at the waist, hurried in boots to the corner-squaring stone and bowed face to face again, walked north to the memorial stone and bent at the waist; one officer reported that all within and without the state was secure, then walked backward to take his place;
translations.idiomatic: Next the Grand General of the Golden Guard bowed face to face and bent at the waist, hurried in boots to the corner-squaring stone and bowed again, walked north to the memorial stone and bent at the waist; one officer reported that all within and without the state was secure, then walked backward to his place;

sentences.zh: 次引文武班就位，揖訖，鞠躬，𣀃鞾急趨入沙墀；

translations.literal: next the civil and military ranks were led to their places; after bowing and bending at the waist, they hurried in boots quickly into the sand terrace;
translations.idiomatic: Next the civil and military ranks were led to their places; after bowing and bending at the waist, they hurried in boots into the sand terrace;

sentences.zh: 次引侍從班橫行，宰相祝月起居畢，分班序立；

translations.literal: next the attendance rank was led across; after the chief ministers finished the monthly salutation audience, they divided ranks and took their places in order;
translations.idiomatic: Next the attendance rank was led across; after the chief ministers finished the monthly salutation audience, they divided ranks and took their places in order;

sentences.zh: 文武兩班出，序立於衙門外。

translations.literal: The civil and military ranks went out and took their places in order outside the yamen gate.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military ranks went out and took their places in order outside the yamen gate.

sentences.zh: 刑法、待制官赴監奏位，中書、門下夾香案侍立，兩省、御史台官、學士、兵部吏部侍郎、金吾將軍、監閣御史並相次出，就衙門外立

translations.literal: Penal-law officials and awaiting-edict commissioners went to the supervised memorial positions; the Secretariat and Chancellery stood attending on either side of the incense table; officials of the two departments, Censorate, academicians, Vice Ministers of War and Personnel, Golden Guard generals, and pavilion-supervising censors all went out in succession and took their places outside the yamen gate
translations.idiomatic: Penal-law officials and awaiting-edict commissioners went to the supervised memorial positions; the Secretariat and Chancellery stood attending on either side of the incense table; officials of the two departments, Censorate, academicians, Vice Ministers of War and Personnel, Golden Guard generals, and pavilion-supervising censors all went out in succession and took their places outside the yamen gate

sentences.zh: （惟學士立門側北候宰相）〉

translations.literal: (only academicians stood north of the gate side awaiting the chief ministers)›
translations.idiomatic: (only academicians stood north of the gate side awaiting the chief ministers)›

sentences.zh: 中書、門下詣香案前奏曰：“中書公事，臣等已具奏聞。

translations.literal: The Secretariat and Chancellery went before the incense table and reported: "As to Chancellery business, we Your subjects have already fully reported it for Your hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Chancellery went before the incense table and reported: "As to Chancellery business, we Your subjects have already fully reported it for Your hearing.

sentences.zh: ”訖，乃退，揖殿出。

translations.literal: " When finished, they withdrew, bowed toward the hall, and exited.
translations.idiomatic: " When finished, they withdrew, bowed toward the hall, and exited.

sentences.zh: 次刑法官、待制官各奏事，並宣徽使答訖，乃出就班。

translations.literal: Next penal-law officials and awaiting-edict commissioners each reported affairs; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service answered each in turn, and they went out to join the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Next penal-law officials and awaiting-edict commissioners each reported affairs; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service answered each in turn, and they went out to join the ranks.

sentences.zh: 次彈奏官、左右史出。

translations.literal: Next the impeachment officers and left and right recorders went out.
translations.idiomatic: Next the impeachment officers and left and right recorders went out.

sentences.zh: 閣內失儀者，彈糾如式。

translations.literal: Those who breached protocol within the pavilion were impeached according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Those who breached protocol within the pavilion were impeached according to the regulations.

sentences.zh: 彈奏官失儀，起居郎糾之；

translations.literal: If an impeachment officer breached protocol, the court diarist corrected him;
translations.idiomatic: If an impeachment officer breached protocol, the court diarist corrected him;

sentences.zh: 起居郎失儀，閣門使糾之；

translations.literal: if a court diarist breached protocol, the Pavilion Gate commissioner corrected him;
translations.idiomatic: if a court diarist breached protocol, the Pavilion Gate commissioner corrected him;

sentences.zh: 閣門使失儀，宣徽使糾之。

translations.literal: if a Pavilion Gate commissioner breached protocol, the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service corrected him.
translations.idiomatic: if a Pavilion Gate commissioner breached protocol, the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service corrected him.

sentences.zh: 凡出者皆𣀃靴急趨揖殿。

translations.literal: All who went out hurried in boots quickly, bowing toward the hall.
translations.idiomatic: All who went out hurried in boots quickly, bowing toward the hall.

sentences.zh: 次中書、門下、學士就位，閣門使宣放仗，再拜，賜廊下食，又再拜。

translations.literal: Next the Secretariat, Chancellery, and academicians took their places; the Pavilion Gate commissioner proclaimed dismissal of the guard; they bowed twice, were granted food in the corridor, and bowed twice again.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Secretariat, Chancellery, and academicians took their places; the Pavilion Gate commissioner proclaimed dismissal of the guard; they bowed twice, were granted food in the corridor, and bowed twice again.

sentences.zh: 次閣門使奏閣內無事，文武官出，殿上索扇，垂簾，輦還宮。

translations.literal: Next the Pavilion Gate commissioner reported that there was no business within the pavilion; civil and military officials went out; on the dais fans were called for, the screens were lowered, and the palanquin returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Pavilion Gate commissioner reported that there was no business within the pavilion; civil and military officials went out; on the dais fans were called for, the screens were lowered, and the palanquin returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 其賜廊下食，自左右勤政門北東西兩廊，文東武西，以北為上立定；

translations.literal: As for the grant of corridor food, from north of the east and west Diligence-in-Governance gates in the eastern and western corridors, civil east and military west, with north as superior they took their standing places;
translations.idiomatic: As for the grant of corridor food, from north of the east and west Diligence-in-Governance gates in the eastern and western corridors, civil officials stood east and military west, with north as the place of honor;

sentences.zh: 中丞至本位，麵南一揖，乃就坐食；

translations.literal: the Vice Censor-in-Chief reached his place, faced south and bowed once, then sat to eat;
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Censor-in-Chief reached his place, faced south and bowed once, then sat to eat;

sentences.zh: 至台吏，讚乃搢笏食，食訖復讚，食畢而罷。

translations.literal: down to the bureau clerks, the intoner praised and then they inserted their tablets to eat; when eating was finished the intoner praised again, and when all had finished eating the ceremony ended.
translations.idiomatic: down to the bureau clerks, the intoner praised and then they inserted their tablets to eat; when eating was finished the intoner praised again, and when all had finished eating the ceremony ended.

sentences.zh: 五月朔，命有司增黃麾仗三百五十人，令文武官隨中書、門下橫行起居，徙翰林學士位於參知政事後，與節度使分東西揖殿出。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, the relevant offices were ordered to increase the yellow-banner guard by 350 men, civil and military officials were made to cross with the Secretariat and Chancellery for the audience salutation, the Hanlin academicians' positions were moved behind the Vice Grand Councillors, and they exited bowing toward the hall, divided east and west with the military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fifth month, the relevant offices were ordered to increase the yellow-banner guard by 350 men; civil and military officials were made to cross with the Secretariat and Chancellery for the audience salutation; the Hanlin academicians' positions were moved behind the Vice Grand Councillors; and they exited bowing toward the hall, divided east and west with the military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 真宗凡三行之，景德以後，其禮不行。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong performed it three times in all; after Jingde the rite was no longer performed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong performed it three times in all; after the Jingde era the rite was no longer performed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗從知制誥李淑議，仍讀時令，詔禮官詳定儀注，以言者謂未合典禮而罷。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong followed the proposal of Drafting Academician Li Shu to continue reading the seasonal ordinances; he decreed that ritual officers work out the protocol in detail, but it was abandoned because critics said it did not accord with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong followed the proposal of Drafting Academician Li Shu to continue reading the seasonal ordinances and decreed that ritual officers work out the protocol in detail, but the plan was abandoned because critics said it did not accord with canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，知制誥宋敏求等言：“奉詔重修定閣門儀制內文德殿殿入閣儀，按今文德殿，唐宣政殿也；

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Drafting Academician Song Minqiu and others said: "By decree we have revised and fixed the Wende Hall entering-the-pavilion rite within the Pavilion Gate protocol compendium. According to the present Wende Hall, it is the Tang Xuanzheng Hall;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining, Drafting Academician Song Minqiu and others said: "By decree we have revised and fixed the Wende Hall entering-the-pavilion rite within the Pavilion Gate protocol compendium. The present Wende Hall is the Tang Xuanzheng Hall;

sentences.zh: 紫宸殿，唐紫宸殿也。

translations.literal: the Zichen Hall is the Tang Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: the Zichen Hall is the Tang Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 然祖宗視朝，皆嘗御文德入閣。

translations.literal: Yet our founding ancestors all held court by entering the pavilion at the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet our founding ancestors all held court by entering the pavilion at the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 唐制，常設仗衛於宣政殿，或遇上坐紫宸，即喚仗入閣。

translations.literal: Under Tang practice, guard of honor was regularly posted at the Xuanzheng Hall; when the emperor happened to take his seat at Zichen, the guard was summoned to enter the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, guard of honor was regularly posted at the Xuanzheng Hall; when the emperor happened to take his seat at Zichen, the guard was summoned to enter the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 如此，則當御紫宸殿入閣，方合舊典。

translations.literal: In this way, entering the pavilion should be held at the Zichen Hall to accord with the old canon."
translations.idiomatic: In this way, entering the pavilion should be held at the Zichen Hall to accord with the old canon."

sentences.zh: ”翰林學士王珪等議：“按入閣者，乃唐舊日紫宸殿受常朝之儀也。

translations.literal: Academician Wang Gui and others deliberated: "Entering the pavilion was the Tang's old rite for receiving regular court at the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Wang Gui and others deliberated: "Entering the pavilion was the Tang's old rite for receiving regular court at the Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 唐紫宸與今同，宣政殿即今文德殿。

translations.literal: The Tang Zichen is the same as the present one; the Xuanzheng Hall is the present Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Zichen is the same as the present one; the Xuanzheng Hall is the present Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 唐制，天子坐朝，必立仗於正衙。

translations.literal: Under Tang practice, when the Son of Heaven held court, guard of honor had to be posted at the main administrative hall.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang practice, when the Son of Heaven held court, guard of honor had to be posted at the main administrative hall.

sentences.zh: 若止御紫宸，即喚正衙仗自宣政殿東西閣門入，故為入閣。

translations.literal: If he held court only at Zichen, the main-hall guard was summoned to enter through the east and west pavilion gates of the Xuanzheng Hall; hence it was called entering the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: If he held court only at Zichen, the main-hall guard was summoned to enter through the east and west pavilion gates of the Xuanzheng Hall; hence it was called entering the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 五代以來遂廢正衙立仗之制。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward the institution of posting guard at the main administrative hall was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward the institution of posting guard at the main administrative hall was abolished.

sentences.zh: 今閣門所載入閣儀者，止是唐常朝之儀，非盛禮也。

translations.literal: What the Pavilion Gate now records as entering-the-pavilion rites is only the Tang regular-court rite, not a grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: What the Pavilion Gate now records as entering-the-pavilion rites is only the Tang regular-court rite, not a grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: ”自是入閣之禮遂罷。

translations.literal: " From this the entering-the-pavilion rite was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " From this the entering-the-pavilion rite was abolished.

sentences.zh: 敏求又言：“本朝惟入閣乃御文德殿視朝，今既不用入閣儀，即文德遂闕視朝之禮。

translations.literal: Minqiu further said: "In our dynasty only entering the pavilion meant holding court at the Wende Hall. Now that the entering-the-pavilion rite is no longer used, the Wende Hall thereby lacks its court-audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: Minqiu further said: "In our dynasty only entering the pavilion meant holding court at the Wende Hall. Now that the entering-the-pavilion rite is no longer used, the Wende Hall thereby lacks its court-audience rite.

sentences.zh: 請下兩制及太常禮院，約唐制御宣政殿，裁定朔望御文德殿儀，以備正衙視朝之制。

translations.literal: We ask that the two drafting institutes and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual institute be directed, following Tang practice for court at the Xuanzheng Hall, to fix the rite for holding court at the Wende Hall on new and full moon days, so as to supply the institution of main-hall court audience."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the two drafting institutes and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices ritual institute be directed, following Tang practice for court at the Xuanzheng Hall, to fix the rite for holding court at the Wende Hall on new and full moon days, so as to supply the institution of main-hall court audience."

sentences.zh: ”學士韓維等以《入閣圖》增損裁定上儀曰：

translations.literal: Academicians Han Wei and others, adding to and revising the "Diagram of Entering the Pavilion," fixed and submitted the court protocol as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Academicians Han Wei and others, adding to and revising the "Diagram of Entering the Pavilion," fixed and submitted the court protocol as follows:

sentences.zh: 朔日不值假，前五日，閣門移諸司排辦，前一日，有司供帳文德殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the month, if it was not a holiday, five days before the Pavilion Gate notified the various offices to arrange preparations; one day before, the relevant offices prepared the pavilion at the Wende Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the month, if it was not a holiday, five days before the Pavilion Gate notified the various offices to arrange preparations; one day before, the relevant offices prepared the pavilion at the Wende Hall.

sentences.zh: 其日，金吾將軍常服押本衛仗，判殿中省官押細仗，先入殿庭，東西對列；

translations.literal: That day, the Golden Guard general in ordinary dress escorted his command's guard; an official deputizing for the Palace Domestic Service escorted the detail guard; they entered the hall courtyard first and faced each other east and west;
translations.idiomatic: That day, the Golden Guard general in ordinary dress escorted his command's guard; an official deputizing for the Palace Domestic Service escorted the detail guard; they entered the hall courtyard first and faced each other east and west;

sentences.zh: 文武官東西序立；

translations.literal: civil and military officials stood in order east and west;
translations.idiomatic: civil and military officials stood in order east and west;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校分入，北向立；

translations.literal: various army officers entered separately and stood facing north;
translations.idiomatic: various army officers entered separately and stood facing north;

sentences.zh: 朝堂引讚官引彈奏御史二員入殿門踏道，當下殿北向立；

translations.literal: court ushers led two impeachment censors in through the hall gate ramp; they stood facing north below the dais;
translations.idiomatic: court ushers led two impeachment censors in through the hall gate ramp; they stood facing north below the dais;

sentences.zh: 次催文武班分入，並東西相向立；

translations.literal: next the civil and military ranks were summoned in separately and stood facing each other east and west;
translations.idiomatic: next the civil and military ranks were summoned in separately and stood facing each other east and west;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校即於殿庭北向立班。

translations.literal: Army officers then formed ranks facing north in the hall courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Army officers then formed ranks facing north in the hall courtyard.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服靴袍御垂拱殿，鳴鞭，內侍、閣門、管軍依朔望常例起居；

translations.literal: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, held court at the Chuigong Hall; the whip was cracked; inner attendants, Pavilion Gate officials, and army commanders performed the audience salutation according to the usual new-and-full-moon practice;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, wearing boots and robe, held court at the Chuigong Hall; the whip was cracked; inner attendants, Pavilion Gate officials, and army commanders performed the audience salutation according to the usual new-and-full-moon practice;

sentences.zh: 次引樞密、宣徽、三司使副、樞密直學士、內客省使以下至醫官、待詔及修起居注官二員並大起居。

translations.literal: next the Military Affairs Bureau, Palace Domestic Service, Three Fiscal Commissaries and deputies, Privy Council direct academicians, Palace Reception commissioners downward to medical officers, awaiting-edict officials, and the two court diarists all performed the great audience salutation.
translations.idiomatic: Next the Military Affairs Bureau, Palace Domestic Service, Three Fiscal Commissaries and deputies, Privy Council direct academicians, Palace Reception commissioners downward to medical officers, awaiting-edict officials, and the two court diarists all performed the great audience salutation.

sentences.zh: 諸司使以下，退排立。

translations.literal: Commissioners of various offices downward withdrew and stood in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners of various offices downward withdrew and stood in formation.

sentences.zh: 帝輦至文德殿後，閣門奏班齊，帝出，殿上索扇，升榻，鳴鞭；

translations.literal: When the emperor's palanquin reached the rear of the Wende Hall, the Pavilion Gate reported that the ranks were complete; the emperor came out; on the dais fans were called for; he ascended the couch; the whip was cracked;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's palanquin reached the rear of the Wende Hall, the Pavilion Gate reported that the ranks were complete; the emperor came out; on the dais fans were called for; he ascended the couch; the whip was cracked;

sentences.zh: 扇開，卷簾，儀鸞使焚香，喝文武官就位，四拜起居；

translations.literal: the fans opened; screens were rolled up; the Ceremonial Guard commissioner burned incense; civil and military officials were called to their places and performed four bows for the audience salutation;
translations.idiomatic: The fans opened; screens were rolled up; the Ceremonial Guard commissioner burned incense; civil and military officials were called to their places and performed four bows for the audience salutation;

sentences.zh: 雞人唱時；

translations.literal: the rooster herald intoned the hour;
translations.idiomatic: the rooster herald intoned the hour;

sentences.zh: 舍人於彈奏御史班前西向喝大起居。

translations.literal: A herald facing west before the impeachment censors' rank called out the great audience salutation.
translations.idiomatic: A herald facing west before the impeachment censors' rank called out the great audience salutation.

sentences.zh: 御史由文武班後至對立位，次引左右金吾將軍合班於宣制石南大起居，班首出班躬奏軍國內外平安，歸位再拜，各歸東西押仗位。

translations.literal: The censors passed behind the civil and military ranks to the facing positions; next the left and right Golden Guard generals were led to combine ranks south of the proclamation stone for the great audience salutation; the rank leader stepped out, bowed, and reported that all within and without the state was secure, returned and bowed twice, and each returned to his east or west guard-escort position.
translations.idiomatic: The censors passed behind the civil and military ranks to the facing positions; next the left and right Golden Guard generals were led to combine ranks south of the proclamation stone for the great audience salutation; the rank leader stepped out, bowed, and reported that all within and without the state was secure, returned and bowed twice, and each returned to his east or west guard-escort position.

sentences.zh: 通喝舍人於宣制石南北向對立。

translations.literal: The announcing heralds stood facing each other north and south at the proclamation stone.
translations.idiomatic: The announcing heralds stood facing each other north and south at the proclamation stone.

sentences.zh: 舍人退於西階，次揖宰臣、親王以下，躬奏文武百僚、宰臣某姓名以下起居，分引宰臣以下橫行，諸軍將校仍舊立。

translations.literal: The herald withdrew to the western steps; next he bowed to the chief ministers and imperial princes downward, bowed and reported the audience salutation of the civil and military hundred officials and Chief Minister [name]'s rank and below; he separately led the chief ministers and others across; army officers remained standing as before.
translations.idiomatic: The herald withdrew to the western steps; next he bowed to the chief ministers and imperial princes downward, bowed and reported the audience salutation of the civil and military hundred officials and Chief Minister [name]'s rank and below; he separately led the chief ministers and others across; army officers remained standing as before.

sentences.zh: 閣門使喝大起居，舍人引宰臣至儀石北，俯伏跪致詞祝月訖，其詞云：“文武百僚、宰臣全銜臣某姓名等言：孟春之吉，伏惟皇帝陛下膺受時祉，與天無窮，臣等無任歡呼抃蹈之至。

translations.literal: The Pavilion Gate commissioner called out the great audience salutation; the herald led the chief ministers north of the ritual stone; prostrate they knelt and finished delivering the monthly salutation address; the text read: "The civil and military hundred officials, Chief Minister [full titles] Your subject [name] and others declare: On this auspicious day of the first month of spring, we respectfully wish that Your Majesty the Emperor may receive timely blessings coextensive with heaven; we cannot contain our joy in shouting and stamping to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion Gate commissioner proclaimed the great audience salutation; a herald led the chief ministers north of the ritual stone, where they prostrated themselves and delivered the monthly salutation. The text ran: "We, the civil and military hundred officials and Chief Minister [full titles], Your subject [name] and others, declare: On this auspicious day in early spring, we respectfully wish Your Majesty may receive the blessings of the season, enduring as heaven itself. We are overcome with joy, shouting and stamping in exultation to the utmost.

sentences.zh: ”歸位五拜。

translations.literal: " They returned to their places and performed five bows.
translations.idiomatic: " They returned to their places and performed five bows.

sentences.zh: 閣門使揖中書由東階升殿，樞密使帶平章事以上由西階升殿侍立；

translations.literal: The Pavilion Gate commissioner bowed and led the Secretariat up by the eastern steps; the Commissioner of Military Affairs and those who held the concurrent title Grand Councillor or higher ascended by the western steps to attend standing;
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion Gate commissioner bowed and led the Secretariat up by the eastern steps; the Commissioner of Military Affairs and those who held the concurrent title Grand Councillor or higher ascended by the western steps to attend standing;

sentences.zh: 給事中一員歸左省位立；

translations.literal: one Supervising Secretary returned to the left department position and stood;
translations.idiomatic: one Supervising Secretary returned to the left department position and stood;

sentences.zh: 轉對官立於給事中之南

translations.literal: the rotation-report official stood south of the Supervising Secretary
translations.idiomatic: the rotation-report official stood south of the Supervising Secretary

sentences.zh: （如罷轉對官，每遇御史台前期牒請。

translations.literal: (If the rotation-report official was dispensed with, each time the Censorate submitted a petition beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: (If the rotation-report official was dispensed with, each time the Censorate submitted a petition beforehand.

sentences.zh: 文官二員並依轉對官例，先於閣門投進奏狀）〉

translations.literal: Two civil officials, following the rotation-report precedent, first submitted memorials at the Pavilion Gate)›
translations.idiomatic: Two civil officials, following the rotation-report precedent, first submitted memorials at the Pavilion Gate)›

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎及刑法官立於轉對官南；

translations.literal: the Vice Minister of Personnel and penal-law officials stood south of the rotation-report official;
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Minister of Personnel and penal-law officials stood south of the rotation-report official;

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎於右省班南，與吏部侍郎東西相向立，搢笏，各出班籍置笏上

translations.literal: the Vice Minister of War stood south of the right department rank, facing the Vice Minister of Personnel east and west, inserted their tablets, each stepped from rank and placed the register on the tablet
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Minister of War stood south of the right department rank, facing the Vice Minister of Personnel east and west; they inserted their tablets, each stepped from rank, and placed the register on the tablet

sentences.zh: （吏部、兵部侍郎以知審官東、西院官充，刑法官以知審刑、大理寺官充）〉

translations.literal: (The Vice Ministers of Personnel and War were filled by the officers who directed the eastern and western Review-of-Appointments offices; penal-law officials were filled by the officers who directed the Review of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review)›
translations.idiomatic: (The Vice Ministers of Personnel and War were filled by the officers who directed the eastern and western Review-of-Appointments offices; penal-law officials were filled by the officers who directed the Review of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review)›

sentences.zh: 親王、使相以下分班出；

translations.literal: imperial princes and commissioners with diplomatic seals downward withdrew by rank;
translations.idiomatic: imperial princes and commissioners with diplomatic seals downward withdrew by rank;

sentences.zh: 引轉對官於宣制石南，宣徽使殿上承旨宣答如儀；

translations.literal: the rotation-report official was led south of the proclamation stone; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, on the dais receiving the imperial rescript, proclaimed the response according to ritual;
translations.idiomatic: the rotation-report official was led south of the proclamation stone; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, on the dais receiving the imperial rescript, proclaimed the response according to ritual;

sentences.zh: 次吏部、兵部侍郎及刑法官對揖出；

translations.literal: next the Vice Ministers of Personnel and War and the penal-law officials bowed face to face and withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: next the Vice Ministers of Personnel and War and the penal-law officials bowed face to face and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 次彈奏御史無彈奏對揖出

translations.literal: next the impeachment censor, having no impeachment to present, bowed face to face and withdrew
translations.idiomatic: next the impeachment censor, having no impeachment to present, bowed face to face and withdrew

sentences.zh: （如有彈奏，並如儀）〉

translations.literal: (If there were an impeachment, all followed ritual)›
translations.idiomatic: (If there were an impeachment, all followed ritual)›

sentences.zh: 引給事中至宣制石南揖，躬奏殿中無事；

translations.literal: the Supervising Secretary was led to the proclamation stone, bowed, and personally reported that there was no business in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Next, the Supervising Secretary was led to the proclamation stone, bowed, and reported in person that there was no business in the hall;

sentences.zh: 喝祗候，揖，西出；

translations.literal: the attendant was called; he bowed and exited west;
translations.idiomatic: the attendant was called; he bowed and exited west;

sentences.zh: 次引修起居注官，次引排立供奉官以下各合班於宣制石南躬；

translations.literal: next the diarist was led; next the attending officials and below were arranged in ranks, each combining at the proclamation stone and bowing;
translations.idiomatic: next the diarist was led; next the attending officials and below were arranged in ranks, each combining at the proclamation stone and bowing;

sentences.zh: 喝祗候揖，分班出；

translations.literal: attendants were called; they bowed and withdrew by rank;
translations.idiomatic: attendants were called; they bowed and withdrew by rank;

sentences.zh: 喝天武官等門外祗候，出。

translations.literal: attendants of the Celestial Martial Guard and others were called to wait outside; then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: attendants of the Celestial Martial Guard and others were called to wait outside; then they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 索扇，垂簾，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭；

translations.literal: fans were called for; screens were lowered; the emperor descended from his seat; the whip was cracked;
translations.idiomatic: Fans were called for, the screens were lowered, the emperor descended from his seat, and the whip was cracked;

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿承旨放仗，四色官𣀃靴急趨至宣制石南，稱奉敕放仗。

translations.literal: a herald received the rescript at the dais to dismiss the guard; the four-color officials hurried in boots to the proclamation stone and declared, "By imperial edict, dismiss the guard."
translations.idiomatic: a herald received the rescript at the dais to dismiss the guard; the four-color officials hurrying in boots rushed to the proclamation stone and declared, "By imperial edict, dismiss the guard."

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍並判殿中省官對拜，訖，隨仗出，親王、使相、節度使至刺史、學士、台省官、諸軍將校等並序班朝堂，謝賜茶酒。

translations.literal: the Golden Guard generals and the acting officials of the Palace Domestic Service bowed face to face; when finished they followed the guard out; imperial princes, commissioners with diplomatic seals, military governors down to prefects, academicians, officials of the Secretariat and Censorate, army officers and commanders, and others all took their places in order in the court hall to thank the emperor for the gift of tea and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Guard generals and acting officials of the Palace Domestic Service bowed face to face; when finished they followed the guard out. Imperial princes, commissioners with diplomatic seals, military governors down to prefects, academicians, Secretariat and Censorate officials, army officers and commanders, and others all formed ranks in the court hall to thank the emperor for the gift of tea and wine.

sentences.zh: 帝復御垂拱殿，中書、樞密及請對官奏事；

translations.literal: the emperor again took his seat at Chui'gong Hall; the Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, and petitioners reported business;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again took his seat at Chui'gong Hall, and the Secretariat, Military Affairs Commission, and petitioners reported business;

sentences.zh: 不引見謝、辭班。

translations.literal: The audience-thanks and farewell ranks were not led in.
translations.idiomatic: The audience-thanks and farewell ranks were not led in.

sentences.zh: 後殿坐，臨時取旨。

translations.literal: For the later session at the rear hall, orders were taken as needed.
translations.idiomatic: For the later session at the rear hall, orders were taken as needed.

sentences.zh: 其日遇有德音、制書、御劄，仍候退御垂拱殿坐，制箱出外。

translations.literal: On days when there were gracious edicts, formal proclamations, or imperial memoranda, one still waited until after the session at Chui'gong Hall, then the proclamation box was brought out.
translations.idiomatic: On days when there were gracious edicts, formal proclamations, or imperial memoranda, one still waited until after the session at Chui'gong Hall, then the proclamation box was brought out.

sentences.zh: 應正衙見、謝、辭文武臣僚，並依御史台儀制喚班，依序分入於文武班後，以北為首，分東西相向，重行異位，依見、辭、謝班序位。

translations.literal: For civil and military officials presenting themselves, offering thanks, or taking leave at the main administrative hall, ranks were called according to Censorate protocol; in order they entered behind the civil and military ranks, with north as head, dividing east and west facing each other, double ranks in separate positions, according to the sequence for audience, farewell, and thanks ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For civil and military officials presenting themselves, offering thanks, or taking leave at the main administrative hall, ranks were called according to Censorate protocol; in order they entered behind the civil and military ranks, with north as head, dividing east and west facing each other, double ranks in separate positions, according to the sequence for audience, farewell, and thanks ranks.

sentences.zh: 餘押班臣僚於班稍前押班，候刑法官對揖出，分引近前揖躬。

translations.literal: The remaining escort officials stood slightly forward of the rank as escorts; when the penal-law officials bowed face to face and withdrew, they were separately led forward to bow.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining escort officials stood slightly forward of the rank as escorts; when the penal-law officials bowed face to face and withdrew, they were separately led forward to bow.

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿宣班，引轉對班見、謝、辭，並如紫宸儀。

translations.literal: A herald at the dais announced the ranks and led the rotation-report rank for audience, thanks, and farewell—all according to Zichen Hall ritual.
translations.idiomatic: A herald at the dais announced the ranks and led the rotation-report rank for audience, thanks, and farewell—all according to Zichen Hall ritual.

sentences.zh: 樞密使不帶平章事、參知政事至同簽書樞密院事、宣徽使並立於宣制石南稍北，宰臣、親王、樞密使帶平章事、使相係押班者，立於儀石南，餘官並立於宣制石南，如合通喚，閣門使引並如儀。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Military Affairs not holding Grand Councillor, the Vice Grand Councillors down to the Associate Signatory of the Military Affairs Commission, and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service all stood slightly north of the proclamation stone; chief ministers, imperial princes, and the Commissioner of Military Affairs holding Grand Councillor who served as escorts stood south of the ritual stone; the remaining officials all stood at the proclamation stone; when summoning was appropriate together, the Pavilion Gate commissioner led them in according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of Military Affairs not holding Grand Councillor, the Vice Grand Councillors down to the Associate Signatory of the Military Affairs Commission, and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service all stood slightly north of the proclamation stone; chief ministers, imperial princes, and the Commissioner of Military Affairs holding Grand Councillor who served as escorts stood south of the ritual stone; the remaining officials all stood at the proclamation stone; when summoning was appropriate together, the Pavilion Gate commissioner led them in according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 讚喝訖，係中書、樞密並揖升殿辭謝，揖，西出，其合問聖體者，並如儀；

translations.literal: When the announcements finished, those tied to the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission all bowed, ascended the dais to take leave and offer thanks, bowed, and exited west; those who should inquire after the emperor's health all followed ritual;
translations.idiomatic: When the announcements finished, those tied to the Secretariat and Military Affairs Commission all bowed, ascended the dais to take leave and offer thanks, bowed, and exited west; those who should inquire after the emperor's health all followed ritual;

sentences.zh: 餘官分班出

translations.literal: the remaining officials withdrew by rank
translations.idiomatic: the remaining officials withdrew by rank

sentences.zh: （彈奏御史候見、謝、辭班絕，對揖出。

translations.literal: (The impeachment censor waited until the audience, thanks, and farewell ranks were finished, then bowed face to face and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: (The impeachment censor waited until the audience, thanks, and farewell ranks were finished, then bowed face to face and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其朝見，如謝都城門外御筵，及召赴闕謝茶藥撫問之類，不可合班者，各依別班中謝對。

translations.literal: For court audiences such as thanking for the imperial feast outside the capital gate, or being summoned to court to thank for tea, medicine, or imperial inquiries—when ranks could not be combined, each offered thanks separately in a special rank.
translations.idiomatic: For court audiences such as thanking for the imperial feast outside the capital gate, or being summoned to court to thank for tea, medicine, or imperial inquiries—when ranks could not be combined, each offered thanks separately in a special rank.

sentences.zh: 賜酒食等並門賜。

translations.literal: Gifts of wine and food were all bestowed at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts of wine and food were all bestowed at the gate.

sentences.zh: 其係正衙見門謝辭，亦門外唱放）〉

translations.literal: For those presenting themselves at the main hall and taking leave with thanks at the gate, dismissal was also proclaimed outside the gate)›
translations.idiomatic: For those presenting themselves at the main hall and taking leave with thanks at the gate, dismissal was also proclaimed outside the gate)›

sentences.zh: 應正衙見、謝、辭臣僚，前一日於閣門投詣正衙榜子，閣門上奏目；

translations.literal: Officials presenting themselves, offering thanks, or taking leave at the main administrative hall submitted a petition to the main hall one day before at the Pavilion Gate, and the Pavilion Gate forwarded the list to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: Officials presenting themselves, offering thanks, or taking leave at the main administrative hall submitted a petition to the main hall one day before at the Pavilion Gate, and the Pavilion Gate forwarded the list to the throne;

sentences.zh: 又投正衙狀於御史台、四方館。

translations.literal: They also submitted main-hall memorials to the Censorate and the Reception Office for Foreign Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: They also submitted main-hall memorials to the Censorate and the Reception Office for Foreign Envoys.

sentences.zh: 應朔日或得旨罷文德殿視朝，止御紫宸殿起居，其已上奏目。

translations.literal: On new-moon days when the throne ordered that the Wende Hall audience be cancelled, only the Zichen Hall audience salutation was held—the list already submitted remained in effect.
translations.idiomatic: On new-moon days when the throne ordered that the Wende Hall audience be cancelled, only the Zichen Hall audience salutation was held—the list already submitted remained in effect.

sentences.zh: 正衙見、謝、辭班並放免，依官品隨赴紫宸殿引，或值改，依常朝文德殿，自有百官班日，並如舊儀。

translations.literal: The main-hall audience, thanks, and farewell ranks were all excused; officials proceeded by rank to the Zichen Hall introduction, or if the schedule changed, they followed the regular Wende Hall court day with the hundred officials' ranks—all according to the old ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The main-hall audience, thanks, and farewell ranks were all excused; officials proceeded by rank to the Zichen Hall introduction, or if the schedule changed, they followed the regular Wende Hall court day with the hundred officials' ranks—all according to the old ritual.

sentences.zh: 應外國蕃客見、辭，候喚班先引赴殿庭東，依本國職次重行異位立，候見、辭、謝班絕，西向躬。

translations.literal: For foreign tribute guests presenting themselves or taking leave, when ranks were called they were first led to the east of the court, stood in double ranks in separate positions according to their own country's ranks, waited until the audience, farewell, and thanks ranks were finished, then bowed facing west.
translations.idiomatic: For foreign tribute guests presenting themselves or taking leave, when ranks were called they were first led to the east of the court, stood in double ranks in separate positions according to their own country's ranks, waited until the audience, farewell, and thanks ranks were finished, then bowed facing west.

sentences.zh: 舍人當殿通班轉於宣制石南，北向立，讚喝如儀，西出。

translations.literal: A herald at the dais announced the rank, turned south of the proclamation stone, stood facing north, proclaimed according to ritual, and exited west.
translations.idiomatic: A herald at the dais announced the rank, turned south of the proclamation stone, stood facing north, proclaimed according to ritual, and exited west.

sentences.zh: 其酒食分物並門賜，如有進奉，候彈奏御史出，進奉入

translations.literal: Wine, food, and distributed goods were all bestowed at the gate; if there were tribute offerings, one waited until the impeachment censor withdrew, then the tribute was brought in
translations.idiomatic: Wine, food, and distributed goods were all bestowed at the gate; if there were tribute offerings, one waited until the impeachment censor withdrew, then the tribute was brought in

sentences.zh: （唯御馬及擔床自殿西偏門入，東偏門出。

translations.literal: (Only the imperial horses and carrying couches entered through the western side gate of the hall and exited through the eastern side gate.
translations.idiomatic: (Only the imperial horses and carrying couches entered through the western side gate of the hall and exited through the eastern side gate.

sentences.zh: 其進奉出入，文武官起居，舍人通某國進奉，宣徽使喝進奉出，節次如紫宸儀）〉

translations.literal: For tribute entering and leaving, civil and military officials performed the audience salutation; a herald announced the tribute from such-and-such country; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service called for the tribute to withdraw—the sequence as at Zichen Hall)›
translations.idiomatic: For tribute entering and leaving, civil and military officials performed the audience salutation; a herald announced the tribute from such-and-such country; the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service called for the tribute to withdraw—the sequence as at Zichen Hall)›

sentences.zh: 候進奉出，給事中奏殿中無事，出。

translations.literal: When the tribute had withdrawn, the Supervising Secretary reported that there was no business in the hall and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribute had withdrawn, the Supervising Secretary reported that there was no business in the hall and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後殿再坐，合引出者，從別儀。

translations.literal: For a second session at the rear hall, those who should be led out followed separate ritual.
translations.idiomatic: For a second session at the rear hall, those who should be led out followed separate ritual.

sentences.zh: 其日，賜茶酒，宰臣、樞密於閣子，親王於本廳，使相、宣徽使、兩省官、待制、三司副使、文武百官、皇親使相以下至率府副率，及四廂都指揮使以下至副都頭，並於朝堂

translations.literal: That day, tea and wine were bestowed; chief ministers and Military Affairs commissioners at the pavilion; imperial princes at their own halls; commissioners with diplomatic seals, the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, officials of the two departments, academicians-in-attendance, deputy commissioners of the Three Departments, civil and military hundred officials, imperial kinsmen with diplomatic commissioner titles down to deputy commandants of the Princes' Household, and the four-brigade commanders-in-chief down to deputy squad leaders—all at the court hall
translations.idiomatic: That day, tea and wine were bestowed; chief ministers and Military Affairs commissioners at the pavilion; imperial princes at their own halls; commissioners with diplomatic seals, the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, officials of the two departments, academicians-in-attendance, deputy commissioners of the Three Departments, civil and military hundred officials, imperial kinsmen with diplomatic commissioner titles down to deputy commandants of the Princes' Household, and the four-brigade commanders-in-chief down to deputy squad leaders—all at the court hall

sentences.zh: （如朝堂位次不足，即於朝堂門外設次）〉

translations.literal: (If places at the court hall were insufficient, seats were set up outside the court hall gate)›
translations.idiomatic: (If places at the court hall were insufficient, seats were set up outside the court hall gate)›

sentences.zh: 管軍節度使至四廂都指揮使、節度使、兩使留後至刺史，並於客省廳。

translations.literal: Military governors commanding armies down to four-brigade commanders-in-chief, military governors, fiscal and transport commissioners' deputies down to prefects—all at the Reception Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors commanding armies down to four-brigade commanders-in-chief, military governors, fiscal and transport commissioners' deputies down to prefects—all at the Reception Hall.

sentences.zh: 詔從所定。

translations.literal: An edict approved what had been fixed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved what had been fixed.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初建明堂，禮制局列上七議：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huizong's construction of the Hall of Enlightened Rule, the Ritual-Regulations Bureau submitted seven proposals:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huizong's construction of the Hall of Enlightened Rule, the Ritual-Regulations Bureau submitted seven proposals:

sentences.zh: 一曰：古者朔必告廟，示不敢專。

translations.literal: First: In antiquity at the new moon one always announced at the ancestral temple, showing that one dared not act alone.
translations.idiomatic: First: In antiquity, the new moon was always announced at the ancestral temple, showing that the ruler dared not act alone.

sentences.zh: 請視朝聽朔必先奏告，以見繼述之意。

translations.literal: We ask that holding court and hearing the new moon always begin with a memorial announcement, to manifest the intent to continue and carry forward.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that holding court and hearing the new moon always begin with a memorial announcement, to manifest the intent to continue and carry forward the legacy.

sentences.zh: 二曰：古者天子負扆南向以朝諸侯，聽朔則各隨其方。

translations.literal: Second: In antiquity the Son of Heaven, leaning on the screen facing south, received the feudal lords; at the new moon audience each faced according to his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Second: In antiquity the Son of Heaven, leaning on the screen facing south, received the feudal lords; at the new-moon audience each faced according to his direction.

sentences.zh: 請自今御明堂正南向之位，布政則隨月而御堂，其閏月則居門焉。

translations.literal: We ask that from now on he take the Hall of Enlightened Rule's due-south position; for issuing governance he should occupy the hall according to the month, and in intercalary months take the position at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that from now on he take the Hall of Enlightened Rule's due-south position; for issuing governance he should occupy the hall according to the month, and in intercalary months take the position at the gate.

sentences.zh: 三曰：《禮記•月令》，天子居青陽、總章，每月異禮。

translations.literal: Third: In the "Book of Rites • Monthly Ordinances," the Son of Heaven dwells in Qingyang and Zongzhang, with different rites each month.
translations.idiomatic: Third: In the "Book of Rites • Monthly Ordinances," the Son of Heaven dwells in Qingyang and Zongzhang, with different rites each month.

sentences.zh: 請稽《月令》十二堂之制，修定時令，使有司奉而行之。

translations.literal: We ask to examine the "Monthly Ordinances" system of the twelve halls, revise and fix the seasonal orders, and have the relevant offices receive and implement them.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to examine the "Monthly Ordinances" system of the twelve halls, revise and fix the seasonal orders, and have the relevant offices receive and implement them.

sentences.zh: 四曰：《月令》以季秋之月為來歲受朔之日。

translations.literal: Fourth: The "Monthly Ordinances" takes the autumn month as the day for receiving the new moon of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: The "Monthly Ordinances" takes the autumn month as the day for receiving the new moon of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 請以每歲十月於明堂受新曆，退而頒之郡國。

translations.literal: We ask that each year in the tenth month at the Hall of Enlightened Rule he receive the new calendar, then withdraw and distribute it to the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that each year in the tenth month at the Hall of Enlightened Rule he receive the new calendar, then withdraw and distribute it to the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 五曰：古者天子負扆，公、侯、伯、子、男、蠻夷戎狄四塞之國各以內外尊卑為位。

translations.literal: Fifth: In antiquity the Son of Heaven leaned on the screen; dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and the barbarian states of the four frontiers each took position according to inner and outer precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: In antiquity the Son of Heaven leaned on the screen; dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, and the barbarian states of the four frontiers each took position according to inner and outer precedence.

sentences.zh: 請自今元正、冬至及大朝會並御明堂，遼使依賓禮，蕃國各隨其方，立於四門之外。

translations.literal: We ask that from now on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and great court assemblies all be held at the Hall of Enlightened Rule; Liao envoys follow guest ritual; tribute states each according to their direction stand outside the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that from now on New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and great court assemblies all be held at the Hall of Enlightened Rule; Liao envoys follow guest ritual; tribute states each according to their direction stand outside the four gates.

sentences.zh: 六曰：古者以明堂為布政之宮，自今若有御劄、手詔並請先於明堂宣示，然後榜之朝堂，頒之天下。

translations.literal: Sixth: In antiquity the Hall of Enlightened Rule was the palace for issuing governance; from now on if there are imperial memoranda or autograph edicts, we ask that they first be proclaimed at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, then posted in the court hall and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: In antiquity the Hall of Enlightened Rule was the palace for issuing governance; from now on if there are imperial memoranda or autograph edicts, we ask that they first be proclaimed at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, then posted in the court hall and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 七曰：赦書、德音，舊制宣於文德殿，自今非御樓肆赦，並於明堂宣讀。

translations.literal: Seventh: Amnesty documents and gracious edicts were formerly proclaimed at the Wende Hall; from now on unless there is an amnesty from the imperial tower, all are to be read aloud at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: Amnesty documents and gracious edicts were formerly proclaimed at the Wende Hall; from now on, unless there is an amnesty from the imperial tower, all are to be read aloud at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.

sentences.zh: 政和七年九月一日，詔頒朔、布政自十月為始。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month in the seventh year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered that proclaiming the new moon and issuing governance begin from the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the ninth month in the seventh year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered that proclaiming the new moon and issuing governance begin from the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 是月一日，上御明堂平朔左個，頒天運、政治及八年戊戍歲運、曆數於天下。

translations.literal: On the first day of that month, the emperor took his seat at the Ping Shuo left bay of the Hall of Enlightened Rule and promulgated the celestial cycles, governance, and the year-cycle and calendrical reckonings for the eighth year, the wuxu year, throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of that month, the emperor took his seat at the Ping Shuo left bay of the Hall of Enlightened Rule and promulgated the celestial cycles, governance, and the year-cycle and calendrical reckonings for the eighth year, the wuxu year, throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自是每月朔御明堂布是月之政。

translations.literal: From this time forth, each month at the new moon he held court at the Hall of Enlightened Rule and issued that month's governance.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forth, each month at the new moon he held court at the Hall of Enlightened Rule and issued that month's governance.

sentences.zh: 先是，群臣五上表請負扆聽朝，詔弗允，至是復再請，始從之。

translations.literal: Previously the hundred officials five times submitted memorials requesting that he lean on the screen and hold court; an edict did not approve; at this time they again requested twice, and then he assented.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the hundred officials five times submitted memorials requesting that he lean on the screen and hold court; an edict did not approve; at this time they again requested twice, and then he assented.

sentences.zh: 十一月一日上御明堂，南面以朝百辟，退坐於平朔頒政。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month the emperor held court at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, facing south to receive the hundred nobles; he withdrew to sit at the Ping Shuo bay to promulgate governance.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month the emperor held court at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, facing south to receive the hundred nobles; he withdrew to sit at the Ping Shuo bay to promulgate governance.

sentences.zh: 其禮：百官常服立明堂下，乘輿自內殿出，負坐斧扆明堂。

translations.literal: The ritual: the hundred officials in ordinary dress stood below the Hall of Enlightened Rule; the imperial palanquin came out from the inner hall; he leaned on the axe-adorned screen at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual: the hundred officials in ordinary dress stood below the Hall of Enlightened Rule; the imperial palanquin came out from the inner hall; he leaned on the axe-adorned screen at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.

sentences.zh: 大晟樂作，百官朝於堂下，大臣升階進呈所頒布時令，左右丞一員跪請付外施行，宰相承制可之，左右丞乃下授頒政官，頒政官受而讀之訖，出，閣門奏禮畢。

translations.literal: The Dasheng music was performed; the hundred officials paid court below the hall; chief ministers ascended the steps and presented the seasonal orders to be promulgated; one of the left and right vice directors knelt and requested that they be sent outward for implementation; the chief minister received the rescript and assented; the left and right vice directors then descended and handed them to the governance-issuing officer; the governance-issuing officer received them, read them aloud to completion, withdrew, and the Pavilion Gate reported that the ritual was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Dasheng music was performed; the hundred officials paid court below the hall; chief ministers ascended the steps and presented the seasonal orders to be promulgated; one of the left and right vice directors knelt and requested that they be sent outward for implementation; the chief minister received the rescript and assented; the left and right vice directors then descended and handed them to the governance-issuing officer; the governance-issuing officer received them, read them aloud to completion, withdrew, and the Pavilion Gate reported that the ritual was finished.

sentences.zh: 帝降坐，百官乃退。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from his seat; then the hundred officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended from his seat; then the hundred officials withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是以為常。

translations.literal: From this it became regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: From this it became regular practice.

sentences.zh: 其歲運、曆數、天運、政治之辭，文多不載。

translations.literal: The texts of the year-cycles, calendrical reckonings, celestial cycles, and governance are for the most part not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The texts of the year-cycles, calendrical reckonings, celestial cycles, and governance are for the most part not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 是後則各隨歲月星曆氣運推移沿改，而易其辭焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter the wording changed with the shifting and revision of the years, months, stars, calendars, and seasonal cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the wording changed with the shifting and revision of the years, months, stars, calendars, and seasonal cycles.

sentences.zh: 初，尚書左丞薛昂條具崇寧以來紹述熙、豐政事，各條其節目，係之月令，頒於明堂。

translations.literal: Initially, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Xue Ang itemized the policies continuing the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms since the Chongning period, listing each article, attaching them to the monthly ordinances, and promulgating them at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Xue Ang itemized the policies continuing the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms since the Chongning period, listing each article, attaching them to the monthly ordinances, and promulgating them at the Hall of Enlightened Rule.

sentences.zh: 尋詔：“頒月之朔，使民知寒暑燥濕之化，而萬里之遠，雖驛置日行五百里，已不及時。

translations.literal: Soon an edict read: "Proclaiming the monthly new moon, so that the people may know the changes of cold and heat, dryness and dampness—even five hundred li a day by relay post to ten thousand li distant already cannot reach in time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict read: "Proclaiming the monthly new moon, so that the people may know the changes of cold and heat, dryness and dampness—even five hundred li a day by relay post to ten thousand li distant already cannot reach in time.

sentences.zh: 其千里外當前期十日進呈取旨，頒布諸州長吏封掌，俟月朔宣讀之。

translations.literal: Beyond a thousand li, they should ten days beforehand submit them for approval; the chief officials of the various prefectures should seal and keep them, awaiting the new moon of the month for proclamation and reading.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond a thousand li, they should ten days beforehand submit them for approval; the chief officials of the various prefectures should seal and keep them, awaiting the new moon of the month for proclamation and reading.

sentences.zh: 御樓肆赦。

translations.literal: Amnesty from the imperial tower.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty from the imperial tower.

sentences.zh: 每郊祀前一日，有司設百官、親王、蕃國諸州朝貢使、僧道、耆老位宣德門外，太常設宮縣、鉦鼓。

translations.literal: On the day before each suburban sacrifice, the relevant offices set places outside the Xuande Gate for the hundred officials, imperial princes, tribute envoys from foreign states and various prefectures, monks and Daoists, and elders; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set up the palace bells and chime-stones and gongs and drums.
translations.idiomatic: On the day before each suburban sacrifice, the relevant offices set places outside the Xuande Gate for the hundred officials, imperial princes, tribute envoys from foreign states and various prefectures, monks and Daoists, and elders; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set up the palace bells and chime-stones and gongs and drums.

sentences.zh: 其日，刑部錄諸囚以俟。

translations.literal: That day, the Ministry of Justice recorded all prisoners to await release.
translations.idiomatic: That day, the Ministry of Justice recorded all prisoners to await release.

sentences.zh: 駕還至宣德門內幄次，改常服，群臣就位，帝登樓御坐，樞密使、宣徽使侍立，仗衛如儀。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession returned to the inner tent at the Xuande Gate, the emperor changed to ordinary dress; the hundred officials took their places; the emperor ascended the tower and took his seat; the Commissioner of Military Affairs and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service attended standing; guard and escort as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned to the inner tent at the Xuande Gate, the emperor changed to ordinary dress; the hundred officials took their places; the emperor ascended the tower and took his seat; the Commissioner of Military Affairs and the Commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service attended standing; guard and escort as ritual.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引群臣橫行再拜訖，復位。

translations.literal: The diplomatic herald led the hundred officials across in two bows; when finished they returned to their places.
translations.idiomatic: The diplomatic herald led the hundred officials across in two bows; when finished they returned to their places.

sentences.zh: 侍臣宣曰“承旨”，舍人詣樓前，侍臣宣敕立金雞。

translations.literal: An attending minister proclaimed "Receive the rescript"; the herald went before the tower; the attending minister proclaimed the edict to raise the golden cock.
translations.idiomatic: An attending minister proclaimed "Receive the rescript"; the herald went before the tower; the attending minister proclaimed the edict to raise the golden cock.

sentences.zh: 舍人退詣班南，宣付所司訖，太常擊鼓集囚。

translations.literal: The herald withdrew to the south of the ranks, proclaimed and handed it over to the relevant office; when finished, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices beat the drum to assemble the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The herald withdrew to the south of the ranks, proclaimed and handed it over to the relevant office; when finished, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices beat the drum to assemble the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 少府監立雞竿於樓東南隅，竿末伎人四面緣繩爭上，取雞口所銜絳幡，獲者即與之。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Palace Manufactories set up the cock pole at the southeast corner of the tower; at the pole top performers on all four sides scrambled up the rope to seize the crimson banner held in the cock's mouth; whoever obtained it received it.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Palace Manufactories set up the cock pole at the southeast corner of the tower; at the pole top performers on all four sides scrambled up the rope to seize the crimson banner held in the cock's mouth; whoever obtained it received it.

sentences.zh: 樓上以朱絲繩貫木鶴，仙人乘之，奉制書循繩而下，至地，以畫台承鶴，有司取制書置案上。

translations.literal: On the tower a wooden crane pierced by a red silk cord, with an immortal riding it, bore the proclamation down along the cord; reaching the ground, a decorated platform received the crane; the relevant office took the proclamation and placed it on the desk.
translations.idiomatic: On the tower a wooden crane pierced by a red silk cord, with an immortal riding it, bore the proclamation down along the cord; reaching the ground, a decorated platform received the crane; the relevant office took the proclamation and placed it on the desk.

sentences.zh: 閣門使承旨引案宣付中書、門下，轉授通事舍人，北面宣云“有制”，百官再拜。

translations.literal: The Pavilion Gate commissioner, receiving the rescript, led the desk and proclaimed, handing it to the Secretariat and Chancellery; it was transferred to the diplomatic herald, who facing north proclaimed "There is a proclamation"; the hundred officials bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion Gate commissioner, receiving the rescript, led the desk and proclaimed, handing it to the Secretariat and Chancellery; it was transferred to the diplomatic herald, who facing north proclaimed "There is a proclamation"; the hundred officials bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 宣赦訖，還授中書、門下，付刑部侍郎承旨放囚，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: When the amnesty proclamation was finished, it was returned to the Secretariat and Chancellery and given to the Vice Minister of Justice to receive the rescript and release the prisoners; the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the amnesty proclamation was finished, it was returned to the Secretariat and Chancellery and given to the Vice Minister of Justice to receive the rescript and release the prisoners; the hundred officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 閣門使進詣前，承旨宣答訖，百官又再拜、舞蹈，退。

translations.literal: The Pavilion Gate commissioner advanced to the fore, received the rescript and proclaimed the response; when finished, the hundred officials again bowed twice, performed the dance, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Pavilion Gate commissioner advanced to the fore, received the rescript and proclaimed the response; when finished, the hundred officials again bowed twice, performed the dance, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 若德音、赦書自內出者，並如文德殿宣制之儀。

translations.literal: If gracious edicts or amnesty documents issued from within, all followed the Wende Hall proclamation ritual.
translations.idiomatic: If gracious edicts or amnesty documents issued from within, all followed the Wende Hall proclamation ritual.

sentences.zh: 其降御劄，亦閣門使跪授殿門外置箱中，百官班定，閣門授宰臣讀訖，傳告，百僚皆拜舞稱萬歲。

translations.literal: For imperial memoranda issued down, the Pavilion Gate commissioner also knelt and handed them outside the hall gate into a chest; when the hundred officials' ranks were set, the Pavilion Gate gave them to the chief minister to read aloud; when finished, it was announced; all officials bowed, danced, and proclaimed "Ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: For imperial memoranda issued down, the Pavilion Gate commissioner also knelt and handed them outside the hall gate into a chest; when the hundred officials' ranks were set, the Pavilion Gate gave them to the chief minister to read aloud; when finished, it was announced; all officials bowed, danced, and proclaimed "Ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 真宗宣制，有司請用儀仗四千人，自承天殿設細仗導衛，近臣起居訖，則分左右前導之。

translations.literal: For Zhenzong's proclamation, the relevant offices requested four thousand ceremonial guards; from the Chengtian Hall a detailed guard was set up to escort; when the close ministers finished the audience salutation, they divided left and right to lead the way forward.
translations.idiomatic: For Zhenzong's proclamation, the relevant offices requested four thousand ceremonial guards; from the Chengtian Hall a detailed guard was set up to escort; when the close ministers finished the audience salutation, they divided left and right to lead the way forward.

sentences.zh: 皇太后臨朝聽政。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager held court behind the curtain and governed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager held court behind the curtain and governed.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年，真宗崩，遺旨以皇帝尚幼，軍國事兼權取皇太后處分。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianxing, Zhenzong died; his final testament said that because the emperor was still young, military and state affairs were jointly entrusted to the Empress Dowager for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianxing, Zhenzong died; his final testament said that because the emperor was still young, military and state affairs were jointly entrusted to the Empress Dowager for disposition.

sentences.zh: 宰相率百官稱賀，復前奉慰，又慰皇太后於簾前。

translations.literal: The chief minister led the hundred officials in offering congratulations; they again advanced to offer condolences; and again offered condolences to the Empress Dowager before the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister led the hundred officials in offering congratulations; they again advanced to offer condolences; and again offered condolences to the Empress Dowager before the curtain.

sentences.zh: 有司詳定儀式：內東門拜表，合差入內都知一員跪授傳進；

translations.literal: The relevant offices worked out the protocol in detail: for presenting a memorial at the Inner Eastern Gate, one Inner Quarters Director should be assigned to kneel, receive, and forward it;
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices worked out the protocol in detail: for presenting a memorial at the Inner Eastern Gate, one Inner Quarters Director should be assigned to kneel, receive, and forward it;

sentences.zh: 皇太后所降批答，首書“覽表具之”，末云“所請宜許”或“不許”。

translations.literal: In rescript replies issued down by the Empress Dowager, the opening wrote "I have read your memorial and noted its particulars," and the closing said "Your request should be granted" or "not granted."
